newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's antitrust opens Generali inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Italy's antitrust opens Generali inquiry.

text.p: Italy's anti-trust authority said on Tuesday it was opening an inquiry into an accord to sell insurance through banks between insurer Generali and banking group Unicredito, even though the accord did not include an exclusivity clause.

Unicredito includes banks and savings banks with a total of 324 outlets in the north eastern Veneto region which, according to the agreement, could hamper competition particularly in the provinces of Belluno, Vicenza and Treviso, the watchdog said in a statement.
These are areas in which Generali has an extensive network of agencies and significant distribution agreements with banks.

The strong increase in the distributive capacity of Generali resulting from the agreement, coupled with the market share it already enjoys in the region, "seems capable of compromising" the level of competition also because of the limited distribution capacity of competitors, it said.
The watchdog said the agreement "could lead to the creation of a significant barrier" to others entering those regions.
It also noted that even without express exclusivity accords banks usually tended to distribute products from one company only.
The banks and companies linked to Unicredito include savings banks Casse di Risparmio di Verona, Vicenza, Belluno and Ancona, Banca del Monte di Rovigo, Cassamarca, and MedioVenezie Banca.
